sources.quote: Once combined, individual and investor-level interlocks reach 13.4% of all companies—including 30.1% of pharmaceuticals and biotechnology companies and 16.9% of all IT and software companies.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: investment-fund employees on competing boards, far more common in pharma/biotech than IT/software. Measures interlocks, not director filings; names no firm. Page also says about 65% of interlocking directors lead PE/VC/investment funds.

notes: No source found counting SEC director filings by investment firms in 2024, or comparing biotech with software on that measure. No source names OrbiMed's or RA Capital's 2024 director-filing counts (16, 21). Named-entity coverage is general: Baker Bros employees on portfolio boards (Bloomberg 2019 via Wikipedia) and RA Capital's claim of 100+ board seats. The closest pattern source is the Columbia Law Review interlocks paper (biotech 30.1% vs IT/software 16.9%), which measures a different thing. The Bloomberg page was paywalled; its content is taken only from the Wikipedia citation.
